statements.status_notes: The advisory's affected code is IterMut::next/next_back, and lru 0.12.5 constructs IterMut through exactly two public APIs: LruCache::iter_mut and the IntoIterator impl for &mut LruCache, which delegates to iter_mut (lru's only other IterMut uses sit in its #[cfg(test)] module, absent from release builds). tantivy 0.24.2 is the lockfile's sole dependent of lru, and its single LruCache - the docstore block cache in src/store/reader.rs - is touched only through LruCache::new, get, put, len and peek_lru. No call to iter_mut or mutable iteration over an LruCache exists anywhere in tantivy or the Apollo workspace (apollo-schema-index's PathNodeIterMut is an unrelated type of its own). With zero instantiations of IterMut in the dependency tree, the compiler emits no code for the generic IterMut::next/next_back, so the unsound code is absent from the shipped binary rather than merely unreachable. lru cannot be moved to the fixed 0.16.3 by a lockfile-only update because tantivy requires lru ^0.12.

lru 0.18.2 fixes this advisory. The bundled copy ships inside py-rattler 0.26.0, which is the newest build installable with conda-rattler-solver 0.2.0 (that solver requires py-rattler below 0.27.0). py-rattler 0.27.0 is published on conda-forge but cannot be installed until a newer conda-rattler-solver release allows it.

RUSTSEC-2026-0253 affects lru's LruCache::pop method. Both Tantivy forks embedded in Milvus use LruCache only through new, get, put, and len; neither invokes pop, and their cache keys are usize values without the advisory's panicking Drop prerequisite. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0253.html, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/bc211a5a76930b120b1eeb25073be27f20ba0387/src/store/reader.rs#L35-L81, and https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/96f3335ab5f061926c5b44cf246e81243e1dedc5/src/store/reader.rs#L72-L118 The milvus-storage bridge in Milvus 3.0 wraps lru 0.16.4 in its GlobalLruCache, which calls get and put only with String keys, so the same conclusion holds there. See https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus-storage/blob/3ae6ac424b8dd3b7dcd06698f6779bb87e269dee/cpp/src/format/bridge/rust/src/cloud_provider_cache.rs

RUSTSEC-2026-0002 (GHSA-rhfx-m35p-ff5j) affects lru's IterMut implementation. Both Tantivy forks embedded in Milvus use LruCache through new, get, put, and len only; neither calls iter_mut, so the vulnerable iterator is not in the executable path. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rhfx-m35p-ff5j, https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/bc211a5a76930b120b1eeb25073be27f20ba0387/src/store/reader.rs#L35-L81, and https://github.com/zilliztech/tantivy/blob/96f3335ab5f061926c5b44cf246e81243e1dedc5/src/store/reader.rs#L72-L118
